This script is to check the sanity of the data generating mechanism. We check the settings where there are no biased expected, and where there are predictable bias.

# Load source file and packages

```{r}
if (!require("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pacman")
}
library(pacman)
pacman::p_load(
  foreach,     # foreach loop
  stats,
  dplyr,
  extraDistr,
  SCCS,
  tictoc,      # Measure performance time
  rio,         # Export file  
  here,
  data.table,
  magrittr,     # To use the pipe %>%
  doRNG,        # Reproducible parallel session
  doFuture
) 


source(here("Codes", "SCCS_sim_functions.R"))
```

# Test each function separately

```{r}
set.seed(2000) 
scen <- scenarios[1,]
test <- generate_full_cohort(n = 100000, obs_time = 500, risk_window_E = 30,
                               p_U = 1e-3, U_on_C = 5, U_on_Y = scen[['UonY']],     
                               p_C = scen[['p_C']], C_on_C = 0.3, E_on_C = 0.2, risk_window_C = scen[['risk_win_C']],
                               p_E = 3.2e-3, C_on_E = scen[['ConE']], E_on_E = 1e-6,
                               baseline_Y = 2e-5, IRR_E = scen[['IRR_E']], IRR_C = 5)

test_reformatted_ignoreC <- SCCS_reformat(data = test, risk_window_E = 30, 
                               risk_window_C = scen[['risk_win_C']], method = "ignore_C")
test_reformatted_excludeC <- SCCS_reformat(data = test, risk_window_E = 30, 
                               risk_window_C = scen[['risk_win_C']], method = "exclude_C")
test_reformatted_censorC <- SCCS_reformat(data = test, risk_window_E = 30, 
                               risk_window_C = scen[['risk_win_C']], method = "censor_C")
test_reformatted_withC <- SCCS_reformat(data = test, risk_window_E = 30, 
                               risk_window_C = scen[['risk_win_C']], method = "adjust_C")
test_reformatted_startE3 <- SCCS_reformat(data = test, risk_window_E = 30, 
                               risk_window_C = scen[['risk_win_C']], method = "adjust_C_obs_at_exp")
test_reformatted_calendar <- SCCS_reformat(data = test, risk_window_E = 30, 
                               risk_window_C = scen[['risk_win_C']], method = "adjust_calendar")

analyse_sccs(data = test_reformatted_ignoreC, rep = 1, method = "ignore_C")
analyse_sccs(data = test_reformatted_excludeC, rep = 1, method = "exclude_C")
analyse_sccs(data = test_reformatted_censorC, rep = 1, method = "censor_C")
analyse_sccs(data = test_reformatted_withC, rep = 1, method = "adjust_C")
analyse_sccs(data = test_reformatted_startE3, rep = 1, method = "adjust_C_obs_at_exp")
analyse_sccs(data = test_reformatted_calendar, rep = 1, method = "adjust_calendar")
```

# Test 0: Setting: no confounding nor mediating effect of C, Approach: ignore C in model

Expect no bias Result: bias -0.00683, relative bias 0.99%, coverage 94.2% (as expected)

```{r}
# Set up parallel sessions
plan(multisession, workers = 32)

registerDoRNG() 
set.seed(2003) 

n_sim <- 500
chosen_risk_window <- 30

tic("Parallel simulation") 

# OR Y -> C = 1 (no effect of C whatsoever) ---------------------------------------------------
test_0 <- foreach(i = 1:n_sim, 
                        .options.future = list(packages = c("extraDistr", "dplyr", "SCCS", "data.table"),
                                               seed = TRUE),
                        .combine = rbind) %dofuture% {
  data <- cohort_time_var_past_e_u(n = 100000, obs_time = 500, risk_window = chosen_risk_window,
                               p_U = 1e-3, U_on_C = 1, U_on_Y = 1,     
                               p_C = 1e-3, C_on_C = 0.3, E_on_C = 0.25,
                               p_E = 3.2e-3, C_on_E = 1, E_on_E = 1e-6,
                               baseline_Y = 2e-5, IRR_E = 2, IRR_C = 1)
  data_SCCS <- SCCS_reformat_confound(data, approach = 1)
  result<-analyse_sccs_confound(data= data_SCCS, rep = i, C_adjust = FALSE)
  result
                        }

toc() # measure run time

bias_quantification(true_IRR_E=2, true_IRR_C=1, result_table = test_0)
#export(test_0, here("SCCS_Simulation", "Results", "Test", "Test_0.csv"))
```

# Test 1: Setting: Only mediating effect of C, Approach: ignore C in model

## 1.1. OR E -\> C = 0.25: Expectation: estimated effect (total effect) smaller than direct effect

Result: downward bias -0.029, percent bias 4.18%, coverage 94.2% (as expected)

## 1.2. OR E -\> C = 5: Expectation: estimated effect (total effect) larger than direct effect

Result: Upward bias, Percent bias 15.9%, coverage 77.8% (as expected)


# Test 3: Setting: Mediating + confounding effect of C, Approach: adjusting for C in model

Expect no bias

Result:

Test 3.1. OR C -\> E = 0.25: bias -0.0085, relative bias 1.23%, coverage 95.4% (as expected), se_gamma_1 = 0.1153

Test 3.2. OR C -\> E = 5: bias -0.005, percent bias 0.71%, coverage 95.2% (as expected)

## 4.6 and 4.7: Effect E on subsequent C = 5 (instead of 0.25)

Result: Bias -0.039, 5.65%, coverage 91.9% (4.6); bias -0.008, 1.167%, coverage 95.5% (4.7)

```{r}

chosen_risk_window <- 28

                        .options.future = list(packages = c("extraDistr", "dplyr", "SCCS", "data.table"),
                                               seed = TRUE),
                        .combine = rbind) %dofuture% {
  data <- cohort_time_var_past_e_u(n = 100000, obs_time = 500, risk_window = chosen_risk_window,
                               p_U = 2e-3, U_on_C = 5, U_on_Y = 5,

  data_SCCS <- SCCS_reformat_confound(data, approach = 4)
  result<-analyse_sccs_confound(data= data_SCCS, rep = i, C_adjust = TRUE)
  result
                        }

toc() # measure run time

bias_quantification(true_IRR_E=2, true_IRR_C=5, result_table = test_4.6)
```

# Test 5: Setting: Confounder U of C and Y and mediating + confounding effect of C, approach: ignore C

## 5.1. OR U on C & U on E = 5

Expect slightly larger bias than test 2 (There is additional confounding effect of U at the first time point, but confounding effect of U in later time points are blocked by C being a collider of E and U)

Result: bias -0.142, 20.5%, coverage 68.6% (quite larger than test 2.1 (-0.072, percent bias 10.49%), potentially due to large effect of U on C and Y)

```{r}
plan(multisession, workers = 30)

registerDoRNG() 
set.seed(2003) 

n_sim <- 1000
chosen_risk_window <- 28

tic("Parallel simulation") 
# OR U>C = 5, U>Y=5 -----------------------------------------------------------
test_5 <- foreach(i = 1:n_sim, 
                        .options.future = list(packages = c("extraDistr", "dplyr", "SCCS", "data.table"),
                                               seed = TRUE),
                        .combine = rbind) %dofuture% {
  data <- cohort_time_var_past_e_u(n = 100000, obs_time = 500, risk_window = chosen_risk_window,
                               p_U = 1e-3, U_on_C = 5, U_on_Y = 5,     
                               p_C = 1e-3, C_on_C = 0.3, E_on_C = 0.25,
                               p_E = 3.2e-3, C_on_E = 0.25, E_on_E = 1e-6,
                               baseline_Y = 2e-5, IRR_E = 2, IRR_C = 5)
  data_SCCS <- SCCS_reformat_confound(data, approach = 1)
  result<-analyse_sccs_confound(data= data_SCCS, rep = i, C_adjust = FALSE)
  result
                        }

toc() # measure run time

bias_quantification(true_IRR_E=2, true_IRR_C=5, result_table = test_5)
export(test_5, here("SCCS_Simulation", "Results", "Test", "Test_5-1.csv"))

```

# Test 7: Setting: Confounder U of C and Y and mediating + confounding effect of C, approach: exclude C and censor C

OR U-\>C = 5, U-\>Y=15:

## 7.1. Exclude C

Result: bias 0.044, relative bias = 6.3% (Interesting that this approach gives upward bias while Censoring C or adjusting for C give downward bias (test 7.2 and 4.2))

## 7.2. Censor C

Result: bias -0.027, relative bias 3.97%
